checked.note: Slice 1 symbol admission: SystemAuthorizationContext contract value object and validation signature; surrounding request-context helpers remain outside this slice.

Slice 3 symbol admission: the TaskContext background-task scope manager -- its constructor, entry/exit protocol, captured-context attributes, principal/tenant resolution, and the system-authorization issuing signature. The surrounding task helpers in core.tasks.* and every task payload they carry remain outside this slice.

Slice 4 symbol admission: the _ReportOutput scheduled-report result contract -- the rendered email body plus the optional attachment content, filename, and MIME type a renderer hands to the archive and delivery steps. Slice 5 adds generate_scheduled_report_task, the scheduled-report task entry envelope: the ScheduledReport id a worker is handed, and the bool | None outcome it reports back -- True or False for a report that was processed, None for a schedule with no resolvable tenant scope. The renderer and helper functions between the two, and the report-provider architecture behind compile_report_context, remain outside this slice; report-provider contracts stay owned by #83.
Slice 1 symbol admission: ResourceAccessDecision contract value object; surrounding tenant/RBAC access helpers remain outside this slice.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the _SCIMAuthenticatedPrincipal protocol and SCIMBearerTokenAuthentication DRF authentication contract -- a Request in, the minimal authenticated-principal/credential pair or None out, and the WWW-Authenticate scheme it advertises. The protocol avoids importing project model classes into the bounded projection; tenant resolution, token validation, IP allowlist, has_perm authorization, and write-flag checks inside the method bodies are unchanged and remain outside this slice.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the _SCIMQuery structural protocol plus every SCIM filter parser/helper function. The runtime values remain Django Q objects, but the checked signatures expose only their combinable query-expression algebra, so the projection does not import django.db.models or the application model graph. The parser functions read no request state and touch no ORM row; their bodies remain behaviorally unchanged.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the two SCIM identifier-boundary functions of the 1.x dual-read window -- identifier_lookup, which answers the model lookup for a legacy integer or opaque UUID identifier, and identifier_lookup_or_none, which answers None instead of raising for an invalid member identifier. get_scim_object_or_404 is deliberately not admitted: it would pull the queryset it scopes into the admission, and queryset-generic typing is a later slice.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the _SCIMAuthenticatedPrincipal protocol and SCIMProviderBearerTokenAuthentication DRF authentication contract for the provider-level SCIM mount -- a Request in, the minimal authenticated-principal/credential pair or None out, over the managing (is_provider) tenant. The protocol avoids importing project model classes into the bounded projection; provider resolution, provider-token scoping, has_perm authorization, and write-flag enforcement inside the method bodies are unchanged and remain outside this slice.

Slice-0 pilot, hardened by Slice 2. Pure SCIM PATCH parsing: no ORM, no request state, no Django imports, so it is clean under the normative flags without depending on django-stubs model inference. Explicit Any values remain only at categorised external-JSON boundaries; absent patch fields use the typed _Unset sentinel.

Slice 6 symbol admission: the _SCIMUserResource, _SCIMMembershipResource, and _SCIMGroupResource structural protocols plus the tenant- and provider-shared SCIMUserSerializer and SCIMGroupSerializer resource contracts. Selected fields and SerializerMethodField return signatures describe the SCIM User/Group JSON boundary without importing application model classes into the bounded projection. The service-provider serializer, context helper, and surrounding ORM/mutation code remain outside this admission; serializer annotations are intended to improve later OpenAPI inference without claiming schema validation owned by #98.
